{{Quote|It was said he could 'sense the future.' His instinctive knowledge of the Force centered him in the present but allowed him to intuit where all possibilities led.|Plo Koon|<ref name="shw1" />}}
'''Tyvokka''' was a [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] who served the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] during the waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. A revered and respected member of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]], Tyvokka trained several [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]], including the [[Kel Dor/Legends|Kel Dor]] [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]]. The Wookiee was renowned for his ability to "[[Precognition/Legends|sense the future]]" and assess the best possible course of action in any given situation, so he was chosen to help [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] broker peace between the [[Stark Commercial Combine]] and the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] during a [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] shortage in [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]].

At the peace summit, which took place on [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]], Tyvokka and Valorum were accompanied by four other [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]: Koon, [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], and Valorum's [[Advisor/Legends|advisor]], [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]]. At Troiken, they rendezvoused with the Federation's representative, [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], and were in turn met by the head of the Stark Commercial Combine, [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark]]. Upon arrival, however, Stark had his men draw their weapons on Tyvokka and his companions, and demanded their immediate surrender. Tyvokka literally turned the tables on Stark and his men, but in the ensuing skirmish, he was accidentally gunned down by Gunray's [[HKB-3 hunter-killer droid|hunter-killer droid]] escort. Eventually [[Death/Legends|succumbing]] to his wounds, Tyvokka's role in the mission was taken by Koon, who was able to secure victory over Stark. Koon would in time take Tyvokka's place on the High Council.

==Biography==
===Crisis===
{{Quote|The underlying problem remains the scarcity of the ''bacta'', and the Thyferrans can offer us no estimate as to how soon they can resume operations.''"<br />"''«Assuming there ''is'' a scarcity of bacta.»|Finis Valorum and Tyvokka|<ref name="shw1" />}}
[[File:Youngdooku.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Tyvokka with [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], and Dooku's Padawan [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]].]]
Tyvokka, a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] who hailed from [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]],<ref name="starships66" /> was a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] who lived during the waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. He trained several [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]], the last being [[Kel Dor/Legends|Kel Dor]] [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]]. By the time Koon's [[Jedi training/Legends|training]] was complete, Tyvokka held a seat on the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]].<ref name="shw1" /> In [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]],<ref name="Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] suffered from a [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] shortage and trouble began to flare in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Since bacta was now rarer, and therefore more expensive, many of the Outer Rim [[Planet/Legends|worlds]] were unable to afford it. However, the newly-formed [[Stark Commercial Combine]] began preying on [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Starship/Legends|ships]], looting their bacta supplies and selling it to the Outer Rim worlds at a cut price. When representatives of the Federation protested to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], it was decided that a [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomatic]] solution would be sought after. As a result, Tyvokka was chosen to be chief negotiator between the two parties.<ref name="shw1" />

Before departing for the summit, the Jedi Master approached his former apprentice, as there was an opening for one of the rotational seats on the High Council, and he wished to put Koon's name forth. At first, the Kel Dor declined the offer, as he believed that there were other [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], such as [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], who were better suited for the position. Tyvokka scoffed at the suggestion, considering Jinn a [[Gray Jedi]], and insisted that Koon was the most suitable candidate for the role. Eventually, the Kel Dor relented and accepted his former master's judgment. Tyvokka then requested that Koon serve as his chief aide during the upcoming summit, and the Kel Dor accepted, suggesting that they bring Jinn along as well in the hope that the Wookiee might be able to part some wisdom to his fellow Jedi Master.<ref name="shw1" />

The pair then met with [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] of the [[Lytton sector/Legends|Lytton sector]],<ref name="shw1" /><ref name="negtc">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> to discuss the details of the summit. Also in attendance were fellow council members [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]], [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], and [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]]. Tyvokka aired his suspicion to Valorum that the bacta shortage may have been a ruse, as it had brought considerable short-term profits to both the [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferrans]] who grew the bacta and the Trade Federation. As a means of validating his theory, Tyvokka suggested that Master [[Tholme/Legends|Tholme]] and his apprentice [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] be sent to Thyferra to investigate. Windu agreed, and at Koon's quiet insistence, Tyvokka declared that in addition to his former apprentice, he would be taking Master Jinn and his apprentice, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], with him to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]] for the summit. Valorum also requested that Gallia accompany them as well, to serve as his personal [[Advisor/Legends|advisor]].<ref name="shw1" />

===Summit on Troiken===
{{Quote|You really don't have any other choices.''"<br />"''«There is ''always'' another choice.»|Iaco Stark and Tyvokka|<ref name="shw2" />}}
Upon arriving at Troiken, Tyvokka, Koon, Jinn, Kenobi, Valorum, and Gallia met with [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] of the Trade Federation, who was accompanied by a guard of [[HKB-3 hunter-killer droid]]s. They were joined by the head of the Stark Commercial Combine, [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark]], who was in turn accompanied by his co-directors&mdash;[[Trodos]], [[Boor-Daa]], [[Tam Gozon]], and [[Lom Portom]]&mdash;as well as an armed guard. As he sat down across a large table from Gunray, Valorum, and the Jedi, Tyvokka suggested that they eschew the usual "preliminaries" of negotiation, and cut straight to what Stark considered to be the solution. Stark agreed, and his associates and guards drew their weapons on Gunray and the Jedi.<ref name="shw1" />

[[File:Tyvokka.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Tyvokka in action during the [[First Battle of Qotile]].]]
Valorum was outraged by the move, and Stark revealed that he was aware of the fact that the summit was in fact a trap meant for him, and that a covert [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Republic paramilitary]] under the command of [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Ranulph Tarkin/Legends|Ranulph Tarkin]] of the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]] was heading for Troiken as they spoke. Valorum was shocked by the development, and insisted that not only was he unaware of Tarkin's actions, but the senator's actions were unauthorized. Stark went on to explain that someone at the summit was aware of the trap since the signal to attack had originated from the meeting hall. He also stated that all of Tarkin's ships had been infected by a [[nanovirus]], and that portions of the fleet would find themselves exiting [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] and going straight into a [[Star/Legends|star]], or a [[Black hole/Legends|black hole]]. The portion of the fleet that would make it to Troiken would be met by Stark's superior forces. Stark then demanded that Valorum, Gunray, and the Jedi all surrender, confident that the Republic would concede to his demands if they did so.<ref name="shw1" />

Tyvokka correctly divined that Stark had planned everything from the beginning, and that the summit itself had been a trap for them. As Stark continued to call for their surrender, Tyvokka grabbed the giant table and flipped it on its side, using it as a shield against Stark's men. As the Jedi leapt into [[First Battle of Qotile|action]], Tyvokka assigned Kenobi to protect Gunray, Gallia to protect Valorum, and Koon to assist him. Using [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], the Wookiee smashed the table and fought Stark's men with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. Jinn urged Gunray to activate his droids and have them assist, but Gunray's vague order to "kill them all" resulted in them opening fire on the Jedi as well. Tyvokka was caught unawares and struck by three [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolts across the chest.<ref name="shw2" />

===Death and legacy===
{{Quote|You&hellip;make me proud&hellip;Plo Koon&hellip;|translated=1|Tyvokka's dying words|<ref name="shw2" />}}
[[File:TyvokkaDeath.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Tyvokka [[Death/Legends|passes away]] with [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] by his side.]]
The skirmish over, Stark and his co-directors fled the hall. Koon tended to the wounded Tyvokka, and requested medical help, but the Wookiee insisted that they move to a defensible position in case Stark returned with more men. As he was helped out of the room by Valorum and Koon, Tyvokka stated that they should make contact with whatever was left of Tarkin's forces and join them, as they had no hope of surviving on their own. The group made it back to the [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class cruiser]] that had brought them to Troiken, and Valorum was able to get through to Tarkin, whom he arranged to rendezvous with at the defensible position of [[Mount Avos]]. While the [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] departed for the rendezvous itself, Koon nursed his former master, who was now slowly [[Death/Legends|dying]]. Due to the limited supply of bacta, Tyvokka was unable to be tended to properly, so he began issuing his final orders. Gallia was to get Valorum off the planet and seek out a diplomatic solution, Jinn was to uncover the details of Stark's nanovirus, and Koon was instructed to rally Tarkin's troops against Stark's onslaught. As his last wish, Tyvokka insisted that Koon take his place on the High Council. The Kel Dor admitted that he did not want Tyvokka to die, but the Master scolded his former apprentice, reminding him of the fifth precept of the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]]: ''there is no death, there is only the Force''. With his dying breath, Tyvokka told Koon that he was proud of him.<ref name="shw2" />

Koon proceeded to take command of the mission. ''En route'' to Mount Avos, the cruiser sustained heavy enemy fire, and was forced to crash land. As a result, the ship exploded after all the occupants had been able to clear it, but Tyvokka's body was unceremoniously incinerated. Koon was disturbed, but Gallia pointed out that the burning wreckage of the ship served as a makeshift [[Jedi funeral/Legends|funeral pyre]] for the late Jedi Master.<ref name="shw3">[[Star Wars (1998) 38|''Star Wars'' (1998) 38]]</ref> What ensued came to be known as the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]]&mdash;the Republic emerged the victors, with Stark being arrested and his collective destroyed. Koon honored Tyvokka's dying wish and took his seat on the High Council.<ref name="shw4">[[Star Wars (1998) 39|''Star Wars'' (1998) 39]]</ref> Several years later, in [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]],<ref name="SW36 date">''[[Star Wars: The Comics Companion]]'' dates the present day events of [[Star Wars (1998) 36|''Star Wars'' (1998) 36]] to [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]].</ref> the Kel Dor reminisced about the conflict with fellow veterans Gallia, Tholme, and [[Jace Dallin]], a member of Tarkin's paramilitary, as well as Master Windu, while telling the story of the conflict to Tholme's new Padawan learner, [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]].<ref name="shw1" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], a picture of Tyvokka, standing alongside the young Qui-Gon Jinn and his master, [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], as well as Yoda, was displayed in a [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] profile of Dooku, who was at that time the leader of the newly formed [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], a group of worlds announcing their secession from the Galactic Republic.<ref name="hnn">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|54|news/1352_1.html|Dooku Spotted in Gree Enclave}}</ref> In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="Chronology" /> shortly before [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] [[Declaration of a New Order|secured himself in office]] as [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] of the first [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], he enacted pan-[[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] killings of the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], known as [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]].<ref name="rots">{{Film|III}}</ref> Koon perished as a result, and Tyvokka was mentioned in a [[Casualty Report: Order 66|report]] to the Emperor, compiled by [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Marcellin Wessel]], in regards to his tutelage of the late Kel Dor.<ref name="o66">{{InsiderCite|87|Order 66: Destroy All Jedi}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Thank you, Plo, for giving me ''another'' opportunity to control my temper.|translated=1|Tyvokka|<ref name="shw1" />}}
[[File:ThreeWookiees.jpg|thumb|right|230px|Tyvokka (right) was one of the most famous Wookiees in galactic history.]]
Tyvokka had no time for excess humility, and he regarded it as being just as poor a trait in a Jedi Knight as excess pride. He was constantly vexed by the modesty and politeness of his final apprentice, Plo Koon, and made sure that he made that clear to Koon himself. Tyvokka was very blunt, airing his opinions and theories in front of others, even when he had no evidence to back his claims. Tyvokka also had little time for more stubborn and independent Jedi such as Qui-Gon Jinn, although he was grudgingly willing to bring the controversial Jedi along with him to the summit on Troiken.<ref name="shw1" /> Tyvokka was also known for his short temper, a trait common among many Wookiees, although the Jedi Master more often than not had the fortitude to suppress his anger.<ref name="starships66" />

Even when mortally wounded, Tyvokka's thoughts were about his mission, rather than his own health. After being hit by blaster fire from Gunray's droids, Tyvokka continued to plan the movements of his team, and shrugged off Koon's insistence that he required immediate medical attention. As he lay dying, Tyvokka still found cause to admonish his student, although his final words to Plo Koon were ones of pride.<ref name="shw2" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|A very ''powerful'' Jedi.|Plo Koon|<ref name="shw1" />}}
Tyvokka's powers were held in high regard by his final Padawan, Plo Koon, as well as his fellow council member, Mace Windu. The Wookiee Jedi Master was said to be able to "[[Precognition/Legends|sense the future]]"; while he was kept focused on the present by his instinctive knowledge of the Force, he was also able to intuit all the possibilities stemming from a given situation.<ref name="shw1" /> This intuition served him well on Troiken, as he was able to determine the depth of Iaco Stark's plotting and resources. Tyvokka was also able to use the Force to destroy large objects, as he demonstrated during the botched summit on Troiken.<ref name="shw2" /> As his weapon, Tyvokka wielded a [[Wood/Legends|wooden]]-handled, [[Curved-hilt lightsaber/Legends|curved-hilt lightsaber]] with a yellow blade,<ref name="negtwt">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> which he utilized during the Stark Hyperspace War.<ref name="shw2" /> The Jedi Master had fashioned the weapon himself, inspired by the crafting techniques used to create his native species' weapon of choice, the [[Bowcaster/Legends|bowcaster]]. To continue the tradition, Tyvokka utilized hardened [[Wroshyr wood/Legends|wroshyr-wood]] in the hilt of his lightsaber.<ref name="starships66" />

==Behind the scenes==
Tyvokka made his first appearance in [[Star Wars: The Stark Hyperspace War|''The Stark Hyperspace War'']], an early arc of the [[Star Wars: Republic|''Star Wars'']] comic line (later retitled ''Star Wars: Republic''). The arc was written by [[John Ostrander]] and illustrated by [[Davidé Fabbri]], and the character also appeared on the cover of the [[Star Wars (1998) 37|second issue]], which was drawn by [[Jan Duursema]] and [[David McCaig]]. He was later drawn by [[Joe Corroney]] for his appearance in ''[[HoloNet News Vol. 531 54]]''.

The ''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]'' incorrectly claims that a "great Jedi Master" died during the [[Fifth Battle of Qotile]]. As the only Jedi Master to have fallen in the Stark Hyperspace War was Tyvokka, this is clearly a reference to him, although ''The Stark Hyperspace War'' shows that he was killed during the First Battle of Qotile.
